title: Jump Tables
concept: A jump table uses function pointer array indexing for O(1) dispatch without branching

steps.title: Defining action functions
steps.explanation:
We prepare action functions with the same signature.

They must share the same signature to be stored in a single pointer array.

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created, preparing the jump table call flow.

steps.title: Declaring the choice variable
steps.explanation:
`choice` represents the index of the function to call.

In practice, this would be determined by user input or state values.

steps.title: Function pointer array (jump table)
steps.explanation:
Function addresses are stored sequentially in the `actions` array.

The target function can be found instantly via indexing.
steps.keyInsight: A function name itself is the function's address.

steps.title: Bounds checking
steps.explanation:
We verify the index is within the array bounds.

Calling without this check risks accessing an invalid address.

steps.title: Calling a function via the jump table
steps.explanation:
`actions[choice]();` immediately calls the selected function.

This eliminates the need for long if-else chains.
steps.keyInsight: A single array index lookup selects the function to execute.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
The program ends with `return 0;`.

Key point: Jump tables are a fast and easily extensible branching pattern.

quiz.question: What is the biggest advantage of a jump table (function pointer array)?
options: All functions can share the same name
quiz.explanation: Even with 100 cases, you can find the function to call with a single array indexing operation, which is much faster than sequential comparison (O(N)) with if-else.

misconceptions.wrong: A function pointer array can hold functions with different signatures (parameters/return types).
misconceptions.correct: No. An array can only hold the same type, so all functions must have the same signature.
misconceptions.why: It is the same principle as not being able to put a float into an int array.

keyTakeaway: Jump tables are a standard pattern for optimizing branching logic in state machines (FSM), command processors, and more.
